pr_title: bench/rttanalysis: make expectation validation fast and sane
pr_body:
This commit reworks the way expectation validation is performed in the
rttanalysis framework. Before this change, we relied on subprocesses to
execute the benchmarks and then parsed the results. This was brittle and
slow. It was also exposed to issues where we still could not parallelize
sub-tests of individual benchmark categories.

We can't rearrange the top-level benchmarks because we want continuity in
the test names. Instead, we introduce a registry pattern which will store
the benchmark cases and then the top-level benchmarks can just exec
themselves from the registry. This does induce some strings, but it seems
worth it. We assert that indeed the benchmark is registered.

This gives us the ability to eschew most (but sadly, not all) of the
subprocess complexity and still get cross-benchmark parallelism. The
subprocess code which remains is about making sure that metamorphic
constants are disabled. It does let us eliminate a bunch of complexity
related to test pattern matching; we now delegate to the go testing
framework to decide which benchmarks to run in the expectation test.
This symmetry is pleasant. It also means that the `--rewrite` flag is now
a bool flag.

The key insight here is that we can use a testing.T and some additional
state to stand in for the previously expected testing.B via an interface.
This works out pretty well.

Fixes #72068
Fixes #71347
Fixes #71107
Fixes #73066

Before:
```
PASS
ok  	github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/bench/rttanalysis	86.593s
```

After:
```
PASS
ok  	github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/bench/rttanalysis	10.620s
```


Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/73097)

@stevendanna maybe I can snipe you into reviewing this given you typed up  https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/71939 and this, in some ways, extends the principles of that change (though is much larger).

Thanks for improving this!

I'm still a bit confused though - how does one rewrite the expectations? I tried running `make bench PKG=./pkg/bench/rttanalysis BENCHES=Revoke TESTFLAGS='-rewrite'`, and although the run "passed", it indicated different numbers for some subtests and didn't rewrite the expectations file. I think it should be reproducible if you pull #68430 and revert the changes to the expectations file.
You don't run the benches to rewrite, you run the test. `make test PKG=./pkg/bench/rttanalysis TESTS=Expectation/Revoke TESTFLAGS='-rewrite'`
